papers.title: A Dynamic Installation of Interference Bushing Method Based on Electromagnetic Driving to Enhance the Joining Quality of <scp>CFRP</scp> Structures
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Stress concentration could easily occur around the CFRP holes under external loads. To improve the fatigue performance of the CFRP joints, this study proposes a dynamic installation of interference bushing (DIB) method based on electromagnetic driving. The effects of the DIB method on the damage characteristics of the CFRP hole and the distribution of the residual stress were investigated through the combination of the experiments and finite element simulations. Additionally, the fatigue life improvement of the TC4/CFRP/TC4 double‐lap bolted joints under different expansion sizes was systematically evaluated. The results show that the damage degree of the CFRP hole increases significantly with the expansion size. Due to the die restricting the axial flow of the bushing material at the installation outlet, more damage was observed at the installation outlet than at the inlet. Because the DIB method generated beneficial residual compressive stress fields in the bushing and laminates, the average fatigue life of joints with 2% and 3% expansion reaches 15.11 and 2.17 times that of joints without expansion. However, at the 4% expansion, severe compressive damage occurred to the CFRP hole, with significant stress concentration at the installation outlet, resulting in a negative fatigue life gain of the specimens.

summary_en.motivation: To improve the fatigue performance of CFRP bolted joints by reducing stress concentration around holes.
summary_en.method: A dynamic installation of interference bushing (DIB) method based on electromagnetic driving is proposed and combined with experiments and finite element simulations.
summary_en.result: The average fatigue life of joints with 2% and 3% expansion reaches 15.11 and 2.17 times that of non-expanded joints, but 4% expansion causes severe damage and negative fatigue gain.
summary_en.validation: Experimental tests and finite element simulations were conducted to assess damage characteristics and residual stress distribution.

papers.title: Titanium alloys for medical applications - A brief review
papers.abstract: Among metallic biomaterials, titanium alloys are a highly reliable option when it comes to ensuring high structural, mechanical and biocompatibility reliability. Its increasing use in the manufacture of medical devices, particularly in the field of orthopaedics, is justified by its mechanical and chemical properties, such as low density, high mechanical strength, high corrosion resistance, low Young's modulus and excellent biocompatibility. The ongoing development of novel alloys, with the aim of obtaining increasingly high levels of biocompatibility, will undoubtedly result in a greater prevalence of this type of biomaterial in future applications. Although there is currently a predominance of type α + β alloys, such as the Ti-6Al-4V alloy, the development of new type β alloys is aimed at achieving greater biological and mechanical biocompatibility. This review aims to provide concise updated information on titanium alloys, their mechanical properties, microstructure, development of new alloys and applications of titanium alloys in the medical field.
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part L Journal of Materials Design and Applications
